questions.question: For $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$, how do the mean and variance compare?
options: mean $np$, variance $np$, so the two are equal

questions.question: For a binomial distribution with fixed parameter $p$, by which factor does the variance change when the number of trials $n$ is doubled?
What is the PMF formula for $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$?
If $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(m,p)$ and $Y\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$ are independent, what is the distribution of $X+Y$?
How is a binomial random variable built from Bernoulli variables?
options: As a sum of $n$ independent Bernoulli variables with the same success probability
As one Bernoulli variable divided by $n$
As the first success time in Bernoulli trials
As a sample drawn without replacement from a finite population of $n$ successes and failures

questions.question: The number of heads in $20$ fair coin tosses has which distribution?
If $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(5,0.2)$, what is $E[X]$?
If $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(4,0.5)$, what is $P(X=2)$?
The number of defective items in $50$ independent items with defect probability $0.02$ is modeled how?
If $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(10,0.3)$, what is $\operatorname{Var}(X)$?
Why does the binomial formula include $\binom nk$?
options: It counts which $k$ of the $n$ trials were successes
It counts trials until the first success
It accounts for sampling without replacement
It gives the probability of one fixed sequence of successes and failures only

questions.question: What assumptions distinguish a binomial model?
options: Fixed number of independent trials with the same success probability
Fixed number of draws without replacement from a finite population
Independent trials with the same success probability until a success
Fixed number of independent trials whose success probabilities differ

questions.question: When can a binomial distribution often be approximated by a Poisson distribution?
options: When $n$ is large and $p$ is small

questions.question: Out of $100$ independent customer contacts, each accepts with probability $0.05$. What distribution models the number who accept?
If $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(3,p)$, what is $P(X=0)$?
If $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(3,p)$, what is $P(X=3)$?
Why is sampling without replacement not exactly binomial in general?
options: The number of draws is no longer fixed in advance without replacement
The trials are dependent because earlier draws change what remains
Items can be drawn more than once, so some successes are counted twice
The binomial applies only to populations that are infinitely large

questions.question: How does $\operatorname{Bin}(1,p)$ relate to Bernoulli?
options: It is First Success with its first trial at one
It is the same success-count model as $\operatorname{Bern}(p)$
It is Poisson with parameter one

questions.question: If $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(100,0.01)$, which Poisson parameter is suggested by the approximation rule?
A variable counts the number of successes before the first failure. Why is this not the binomial model as stated?
options: The number of trials is not fixed in advance
Success and failure are binary outcomes on each trial
